summary: Elevated 5xx rate for ClearPath during priority-queue fairness imbalance causing runtime failovers
description:
Issue summary:
ClearPath reported a sustained increase in 5xx responses for a subset of API requests tied to their tenant during a period of steady medium concurrency. Symptoms included 502/503 responses from the API Gateway and rapid cycling of several serving-runtime instances for the tenant group.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: intermittent failed requests for embedding and chat endpoints (~3-8% error rate over a 45-minute window).
- Affected customers: ClearPath Analytics (enterprise) — business reports degraded UX and automated ingestion failures.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east-1 region.
- Tier: enterprise tenant pinned to redwood-rlhf-legacy model with fallback to gpt-medium-8k.

Steps to reproduce (reported by CS):
1) Replay customer production traffic at ~120-150 RPS with same request distribution (short chat + embedding bursts).
2) Observe 5xx increase after ~10-20 minutes concentrated on requests routed to tenant priority queue.
3) Runtime logs show repeated graceful-drain and restart cycles for some worker processes.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returns 502/503 for a subset of streaming and sync requests.
- Serving-runtime processes for tenant enter graceful-drain repeatedly, then fail health checks and are restarted.
- KV cache eviction spikes prior to the first failures.

Expected behavior:
- Traffic shaper and priority queue should preserve fairness; runtime instances should not repeatedly fail during steady-state medium concurrency.

Immediate logs / snippets (redacted):
- apigw: "upstream returned 502, host=runtime-xxxx; queue_wait_ms=842"
- runtime: "[WARN] draining due to priority-seat starvation; inflight=128; max_inflight=256"
- runtime: "OOM-like memory pressure detected in tenant sandbox; heap_used=1.8GB; restart scheduled"

Initial hypothesis:
- Priority-queue fairness imbalance caused head-of-line blocking for lower-priority work which increased request latencies. Increased inflight requests caused KV cache thrash and higher memory churn in the tenant sandbox, triggering runtime health failures and restarts which propagated 502/503s through the API Gateway.

Workarounds attempted by Support/Oncall:
- Short-term: temporarily raised per-tenant concurrency cap for ClearPath to smooth request queuing (apigw policy) and routed a percentage of traffic to fallback model variant.
- Restarted affected runtime pool with staggered backoff and increased socket backlog.
- Flushed a small KV cache partition serving the tenant to reduce eviction storm.

Next steps planned:
- Deploy a scheduler patch to better rebalance priority queues and avoid starvation (PR linked).
- Add a metric for per-tenant queue-age to alert earlier.
- Postmortem and runbook update with recommended per-tenant knobs.

investigation_notes:
Timeline summary: 09:10 alert from ClearPath; 09:25 repro harness validated queue_wait and runtime drain; 09:40 increased per-tenant cap and restarted runtimes; 10:05 observed error rate decline; 13:40 hotfix PR created; 02:22 next-day canary validated.

Findings:
- The apigw priority queue implementation allowed a small set of long-lived high-priority requests to monopolize execution windows under this tenant traffic pattern (fairness weight enforcement bug).
- When priority-starvation occurred, request latencies pushed more in-flight contexts into the runtime which caused accelerated KV cache eviction; this amplified memory churn in tenant sandboxes (small memory leak in legacy model path) and triggered health restarts.

Evidence:
- Per-tenant queue_wait histogram and runtime heap usage graphs (links attached in Confluence).
- Similarity to SUP-62111 noted in linked_issues — same tenant-level throttling patterns but different root cause.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: increased per-tenant concurrency cap, flushed tenant KV partition, and performed staggered runtime restarts which brought immediate error rates down to <=1%. Hotfix (scheduler weight adjustment) merged and canaried (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2481).

Permanent fix: scheduler change to enforce stricter fairness and a follow-up runtime patch to close the small memory leak in the legacy model path scheduled for 2026-03-20 deployment.

Post-incident actions:
- Create an alert on per-tenant queue_age > 250ms.
- Update runbook with steps to increase per-tenant cap and trigger graceful restart sequence.
- Inform Customer Success to follow up with ClearPath for impact credit discussion if requested.

Ticket status: Resolved (mitigation verified in canary and prod); postmortem in progress.
